corpus.rule: one entry per finding id; an id recorded in several audit files takes the last file in sorted order (as matrix/build_matrix.py)

semantics_xref.status: final ids: each root cause names the axioms (AX-NN) it violates and the mechanism (M-NN) its remedy needs; member_classes counts the semantics lane's own classes of its members

root_causes.title: Graph scope is added by hand to each statement
root_causes.statement: Graph isolation is a column or first subscript that every query, join, walk, procedure and writer must add for itself; there is no graph-scoped access layer. Readers and writers that omit the predicate (all-graphs walks, joins by id across graphs, schema procedures under USE GRAPH, the SQL adapter, sample servers, native readers, reifier deletion) answer with, or change, another graph's content.

violates.other: SYS-D3/SYS-D4 (each datum belongs to one graph; a call that names no graph uses the default graph); CONTEXT.md:38-43 (an all-graphs read is the union of each graph's own answer)

root_causes.remedy: Route every read and write through one graph-scoped access layer whose statements always bind graph_id (default '') and join on (graph_id, id); refuse unscoped calls; give every reader's tests a two-graph fixture with one id held by both graphs.

root_causes.title: Stored facts whose key omits the graph
root_causes.statement: Several stores key a fact without its graph: ledger node records (genesis and LedgerApply record nodes graph-blind), reifier nodes (always the default graph), BM25 and IVF indexes with no recorded graph, edge vectors in a snapshot. Ownership checks built on them (redaction's targets, liveness, verify(), node-delete existence, index use under a graph) cannot attribute the fact, so they attribute it to the default graph or to every graph.

violates.other: SYS-D3 (each piece of data belongs to one graph); ADR-0013/plan.md:9-10 (node records are graph-blind by design)

root_causes.remedy: Make the graph part of every stored key: record each node record's graph, create reifiers in the edge's graph, record the graph of every derived index and archive row; treat an absent graph as unknown (refuse or report incomplete), never as the default graph.

root_causes.title: Removal reach is not derived from a declared store inventory
root_causes.statement: Erasure, redaction's liveness and reach, snapshot export and the redaction receipt each list by hand the stores and fields they cover. Stores and fields outside those lists keep an erased or redacted tenant's content and the receipt does not name them: IVF/tree/PLAID and BM25 indexes, temporal-only edges, routed vectors, embedding_quarantine, legacy Graph_KG ledger rows after an upgrade, IVG's own snapshot archives, the metadata of a revision that recorded nothing, and the audit's target digest.

violates.other: SYS-D26 (erasure removes content from every store); ADR-0004; spec 256 US1/SC-001 and FR-008 (the receipt names what it does not reach)

root_causes.remedy: Declare one store inventory (each store and field with its owning graph/tenant key and its erase, redact, export and liveness hooks) and generate erasure, LiveRows/Matches, the snapshot plan and the receipt's out_of_reach list from it; check mechanically that every writer's target store is in the inventory.

root_causes.title: Erase, ledger commits and redaction start are not serialized on the ledger head lock
root_causes.statement: The eraser deletes rows and kills statement-map entries without ^IVG.Ledger("head"); redaction reads its 'another run?' check and its liveness check unlocked and READ UNCOMMITTED and sets its marker only with the first tombstone; adoption and the first enable read the state they decide on before taking the lock. Each is a check-then-act on ledger-owned facts that a concurrent commit, erasure, rollback or second run invalidates.

violates.other: LED-B4.14.4 (only the head-lock holder changes the statement maps); RED-B1.1 (never tombstone live content); premises P-1311, P-C01, P-A3 (false at the pin)

root_causes.remedy: Serialize erase, ledger commits, adoption, enable and redaction start on the head lock (HD-1201 and HD-1301 working answers): take the lock before reading what a step decides on, check liveness against committed state and set the per-target marker in the same locked step, run the eraser's row deletes and statement cleanup under the same lock, and let Final act only when its scan reached the head it holds.

root_causes.title: Unlocked read-modify-write of shared facts outside the ledger
root_causes.statement: Outside the ledger, writers of shared facts read, decide and write with no lock, or under a lock mode that excludes nothing: multigraph mode off vs a parallel-edge write, BM25 Build/Drop, adjacency rebuilds (shared ^IVG.AdjW), native-plan DropAll vs Build, embed-queue claims, ledger_stats counters (%OpenId/%Save), snapshot file names.

violates.other: playbook §1 principle 3 (concurrency control lives in the database; lock plans are proved per handler)

root_causes.remedy: Give every handler a lock plan: each read-modify-write of a shared fact holds the owner's exclusive lock across the read and the write, or uses an atomic primitive ($Increment, unique names, a version-checked write); one two-process interleaving test per handler.

root_causes.title: Derived stores and caches have no reliable staleness signal
root_causes.statement: Caches and rebuilt stores (degree cache, algorithm cache, BM25 indexes, the interned snapshot ^NKG, temporal bucket aggregates, an engine's multigraph-mode cache) are kept current by a token or generation that is stepped after the write, killed and restarted, not stepped on every path (weights, node-only writes, temporal writes), survives a rollback ($Increment), or is not consulted at all, so a derived answer stays 'current' after its source changed or rolled back.

violates.other: CONTEXT.md:109-120 (graph-version token); ADR-0012; AlgoCache.cls:5-7 ('never wrongly fresh')

root_causes.remedy: One staleness mechanism for every derived store: a monotonic per-graph epoch stepped before every source write on every path and never killed, recorded at build and compared at read; mark the derived store stale on rollback, or store a computed answer only when the writer lock was free and the epoch did not move.

root_causes.title: Multi-call readers have no consistency protocol
root_causes.statement: Readers that span several calls check the redaction marker once before reading, and save_snapshot reads every store READ UNCOMMITTED with no epoch, so a reader can return a partially redacted view and an archive can hold writes that never commit.

violates.other: HD-1401 (a reader returns a consistent view or the documented in-progress result); HD-1802 (a consistent snapshot needs quiet writers or an epoch); IRIS contract E-VIS

root_causes.remedy: Validate every multi-call read against an epoch (bumped by each redaction batch and Final and by writers) after the read and retry or refuse on change; for exports, an export gate that writers respect or a refusal while transactions are open.

root_causes.title: The ledger is not the single writer of governed content
root_causes.statement: Ledger-governed content has many writers besides the ledger (bulk loader, purges and row drops, direct edge deletes, GraphQL mutations, bulk_delete_adjacency, temporal writes, server writers, raw SQL), and strict mode is a per-engine cached client check (5 s TTL, fail-open). So writes reach governed content unrecorded, leave live statement entries for removed rows, and are not refused by a redaction's marker.

violates.other: spec 213 FR-047; premises P-C02 and P-L6 (false at the pin); HD-1103 (strict mode is client-side)

root_causes.remedy: Enforce ownership in the server: one write gate (Txn_Begin or the content tables' row hooks) that every content writer passes, which refuses ungoverned writes under strict mode and writes into a marked target, decided per write and fail-closed; the writer census becomes its test list.

root_causes.title: Retries re-execute effects the idempotency record does not cover
root_causes.statement: Idempotency covers only the revision: post-commit properties are a separate write that a replay applies again, a replay rebuilds its answer without statement ids, and the HTTP client and the Cypher server resend a write after an ambiguous outcome. A retry can therefore save twice or revive erased content.

violates.other: spec 213 ledger-api.md:26 (a replay returns the original outcome); HD-1305, HD-1603, HD-1702

root_causes.remedy: Put the whole effect under the idempotency record (post-commit properties recorded with the revision and skipped on replay; the stored first answer returned) and retry only reads or writes known not to have started; answer 'outcome unknown' otherwise.

root_causes.title: A command's writes are not one validated, all-or-nothing unit
root_causes.statement: Multi-step and multi-store commands run in several transactions or autocommit statements (bulk loader chunks, the FHIR event route, the Neo4j commit route, FHIR Register and Schedule, reifier cleanup, temporal-index writes), and some refusals are detected after the first write (index-handle build, store_embeddings routes, a refused temporal write), so a failure or refusal leaves part of the command applied.

violates.other: USER_GUIDE.md:238-241 (each bulk write is a transaction); Neo4j commit-route and Bolt transaction semantics (P-1612)

root_causes.remedy: One write-transaction wrapper used by every entry point: validate the whole request first, then perform every write of the command in one transaction (nesting with TROLLBACK 1), never committing inside it; a failure test per entry that asserts no store changed.

root_causes.title: IVG ObjectScript writers roll back their caller's transaction
root_causes.statement: Some ObjectScript writers (adjacency sync/rebuild, BM25 Insert/Delete) handle a failure with TROLLBACK, which ends every level, instead of the nesting discipline the Python path follows; a failing IVG call inside a caller's transaction discards the caller's own work.

violates.other: CHANGELOG 4.6.4 and _write_txn.py:1-30 (an IVG write nested in a caller's transaction undoes only its own level); IRIS contract E-PARTIAL

root_causes.remedy: One Txn helper for every ObjectScript writer that rolls back only the level it opened (TROLLBACK 1, and only when it started one); a nested-failure test per writer.

root_causes.title: Environment premises are asserted, not validated
root_causes.statement: The product relies on engine, edition, driver and optional-library behaviour it neither probes at run time nor tests on the configurations it supports: SQL COMMIT/ROLLBACK ending every level (true only as 'measured on 2026.3'), durability of an acknowledged commit with SynchCommit=0, the uv.lock driver 5.3.2 (Decimal scores, <LIST ERROR> duplicate reports, closed cursors), VECTOR_L2 on Community, %AI classes in the test deploy, rdflib's API, the Arno library's presence and build, IRIS's default schema for unqualified names.

violates.other: playbook §1 principle 2 (model the environment's freedom; state each narrower premise and test it); SYS-P1..SYS-P4 are stated premises

root_causes.remedy: An executable environment contract for every supported (engine, edition, driver, optional library) cell, run in CI, plus run-time capability probes that refuse with a named reason instead of assuming; a driver floor in pyproject.toml with a refreshed uv.lock.

root_causes.title: The IVG Schema name is not resolved from one source
root_causes.statement: The namespace's schema record is the intended single source of the IVG Schema name, but legacy SQL files, the 4.0.0 upgrade, the bulk loader's index rebuild, setup's DROP INDEX and the sample API hard-code Graph_KG or unqualified names, and the first-use check accepts a namespace with no record.

violates.other: ADR-0016 (the schema chosen at install is followed by everything); spec 262 FR-001/FR-006a/FR-007

root_causes.remedy: Derive every SQL name through one qualifier from the deploy record (engine._ivg_schema); refuse a namespace with no record; retire or regenerate the legacy SQL files; run the suites on a non-default-schema namespace.

root_causes.title: Failures are swallowed into empty, default or success answers
root_causes.statement: Handlers catch failures and answer as if nothing happened: [] for a failed read, False ('exists') for a refused write, DONE for a failed embedding, success with failed rows, 'healthy' with no database, zero vectors for a failed lookup, a fused search without its failed leg, a restore that drops a line it cannot write. The outcome is not computed from the operation's result.

violates.other: CHANGELOG 4.6.0 rule 'a failed read raises'; 4.7.0 row 14 (every bulk writer raises for a refused row); 4.6.0 R265 (no silent empty answer)

root_causes.remedy: Enforce the 4.6.0 rule mechanically: no handler returns an empty/default answer from an except clause; every outcome (removed, DONE, restored counts, health, legs used) is computed from the operation's own result; a lint over except clauses plus a fault-injection test per reader.

root_causes.title: Refusals are not mapped to one typed error hierarchy at the boundary
root_causes.statement: Each layer raises its own exception types and messages: lexer SyntaxError, ValueError from the translator, connection failures reported as client syntax errors, node_not_found decoded as a relationship failure, wrong reasons in messages, SDK calls that skip the 401/403 map, the metrics hook missing Python-side refusals.

violates.other: errors.py:1-17 (one catchable root IVGError); USER_GUIDE.md:313-318 (CypherParseError, GraphWriteError)

root_causes.remedy: One error mapping per boundary (parser, write path, HTTP status, SDK, wire decoder): every refusal is a subclass of IVGError carrying the server's reason code, transport failures are transient errors; a test that enumerates every exported exception class and server code.

root_causes.title: The Cypher and AQL translators have no reference semantics
root_causes.statement: The translators rewrite each clause shape into SQL locally, with no reference evaluator to compare against; shapes outside the tested ones (literal-endpoint CREATE, FOREACH over a parameter, MERGE ON SET shapes, UNWIND..WITH, empty aggregates, null SET, '//' in strings, inline relationship properties, per-row MERGE SET, shortcut texts matched by substring) give wrong answers or errors.

violates.other: openCypher semantics and the TCK (docs/dev/TCK.md); CYP-B6.x; KNOWN_ISSUES.md

root_causes.remedy: Drive the translators from a reference semantics: the typed openCypher TCK at the pin on every supported engine, a differential oracle per clause shape against a reference evaluator, and a refusal for every shape outside the covered set.

root_causes.title: Stored values carry no type
root_causes.statement: Property and qualifier values are stored as JSON text or native subscripts with no type tag and no single serializer, so numbers and strings compare as each other, floats come back as integers, NaN is stored as JSON no reader accepts, canonical label forms are not JSON, native index values return as text, and a filter matches stored JSON text.

violates.other: playbook §1 principle 7 (typed ids and values); spec 255 (a value comes back with the type it was written with); spec 204 FR-012

root_causes.remedy: A typed value encoding shared by every writer and reader (the planned typed storage), one JSON serializer (allow_nan=False) for qualifiers and label sets, and the TCK typed runs on mixed data.

root_causes.title: Domain codes, units and metrics are untyped
root_causes.statement: Kinds, modes, time units, metric names and fusion weights are raw strings or numbers: any revision kind is accepted, any compile-mode value acts as sync, 'now' is computed in seconds for a millisecond index, a missing time becomes 0, 'cosine' is an unnormalised dot product, an L2 distance is ranked as a similarity, default weights go to legs by position.

violates.other: playbook §1 principle 7 (enums, not codes; typed values); NAT-X12; LED-B4.9.2

root_causes.remedy: Enums for kinds and modes that refuse unknown values, a unit carried by each temporal index, metric objects that carry normalisation and sort direction, weights keyed by leg kind; one unit test per value of each enum.

root_causes.title: Query text is built by pasting values
root_causes.statement: The AQL translator pastes literals into Cypher text and a dotted function name is pasted into SQL, so caller text rewrites the query (and execute_aql has no read-only switch).

violates.other: CYP-I9.4 (a name in a query reaches SQL only as a bound value or a checked name); CYP-I8.6 (read-only changes nothing)

root_causes.remedy: Bind every literal as a parameter, validate identifiers against a grammar or an allow-list, and apply read_only at every query entry including execute_aql.

root_causes.title: No server-side authorization or exposure boundary
root_causes.statement: Protection rests on documentation, client flags or the start-up path: file and global helpers are callable by a reading role, ImportGlobals skips the allow-list, Bolt binds every interface unless started by the CLI, the CLI binds 0.0.0.0 with no key, demo write routes need no key, the executor checks no privilege, the installer creates no least-privilege user.

violates.other: no SYS-I axiom covers it (an ontology gap); HD-1601 (the namespace is the authorization boundary); ADMIN_GUIDE.md:450-473 (least-privilege reading role); deploy/README.md:86

root_causes.remedy: Decide the boundary (HD-1601) and enforce it in the server: no file or global helpers reachable by reading roles, loopback default bind and a refusal of unauthenticated external binds in the app itself, the key middleware on every server, a privilege check in the executor (or a documented resource boundary), an installer that creates the least-privilege user.

root_causes.title: Edge identity for parallel edges is not one rule
root_causes.statement: Multigraph support (spec 234) was implemented on some paths only: single-edge writers guard the triple only when ekey is 0, verify_graph and the graph check compare rows to keyed counts per triple wrongly, Bolt and the ledger identify an edge by its triple, in-degree collapses parallel edges that out-degree counts.

violates.other: spec 234 FR-002/FR-007/FR-012/FR-013, SC-005; CONTEXT.md:103-108 (parallel edges each count)

root_causes.remedy: One edge identity (s, p, o, ekey) used by rows, adjacency counts, the ledger, Bolt ids, degree and verify, with spec 234's ambiguous-tuple refusal where only a triple is given; a multigraph fixture in each reader's tests.

root_causes.title: Derived-row marks are ordinary qualifier keys with no single predicate
root_causes.statement: Whether an edge row is derived (temporal-backed, or inferred) is recorded as an ordinary qualifier key that any caller, the ledger included, can also write ('temporal', 'inferred'), and is tested by different predicates in the deleters, the ledger and the Python mirror; the adopt/retract step runs on some writers only (store_edge does not adopt; Purge leaves marked rows; create_edge adopts after its commit). Governed and explicit rows are therefore deleted as derived ones, and derived rows survive as explicit ones.

violates.other: ADR-0009 and its amendment; HD-0302; ADR-0015; schema.py:3187 (retract_inference deletes only what materialize_inference wrote)

root_causes.remedy: One shared mark that no caller can write (a reserved key refused by every writer and the ledger, or a column), one predicate, and one adopt/retract step called by every writer and deleter inside its own transaction.

root_causes.title: Results depend on storage order or join multiplicity
root_causes.statement: Result prefixes (TOP n) without a total ORDER BY, TOP 1 over several qualifying rows, statement-id allocation in scan order, schema procedures sampling one element, tie handling in shadow mode, and label joins that repeat a node make answers a function of storage order or join shape.

violates.other: playbook §1 principle 5 (never depend on storage or insertion order, only on keys and explicit orderings); gate 3.4-storage-order

root_causes.remedy: Order every result prefix and every allocation by a total key, use EXISTS for filters, and close the storage-order scan's candidate list (order or document each).

root_causes.title: Identity by a non-injective checksum
root_causes.statement: Compiled plan classes and the interpreter's used-relationship set are keyed by a 32-bit $ZCRC, so two shapes share one class and two relationships count as one; a build then marks whatever entry the hash holds.

violates.other: ADR-0014:19 (a compiled class answers exactly as the interpreter does); NAT-B1.11; NAT-I3

root_causes.remedy: Key plans and relationships by an exact key or a collision-resistant digest (the SHA-256 already computed), and keep the shape check under the entry's lock.

root_causes.title: Restore writes stores directly instead of through their owners
root_causes.statement: save_snapshot/restore_snapshot copy rows and globals wholesale: a replacing restore lays an archive's ledger over the live one, a merge guards plain tables on their first column only and overwrites temporal aggregates, and the adjacency index is written outside its one writer. The stores' own invariants are not maintained.

violates.other: spec 213 FR-043 (the ledger survives a snapshot); ADR-0011 (one adjacency writer); SNP-B4.x (merge by the row's own key)

root_causes.remedy: Restore through the owners: refuse an archive whose ledger history does not extend the live one before any mutation, rebuild derived stores (adjacency, aggregates) from restored rows, and guard each merged table on its primary or unique key.

root_causes.title: Vector identity is enforced per seam and fails open
root_causes.statement: Each vector-writing seam (engine writes, Python embedder fallback, the IRIS queue worker, VectorOptimizer, enqueue, upgrade placement, kg_KNN_VEC's route guard) implements its own identity and route check, some none, and a failed registry read turns the check off.

violates.other: ADR-0006 (every seam that writes vectors consults the registry); spec 226 FR-014 (enforcement is not opt-in); spec 227

root_causes.remedy: One vector-write gate in the server that every seam calls: it resolves the (graph, model, kind) route, compares identity and width, and fails closed when the registry cannot be read.

root_causes.title: Input validation is per entry point, not at the shared write boundary
root_causes.statement: Each entry point validates its own input, so graph names, timestamps and weights, vector widths and duplicates, the reserved stopword name and the wire schema's length limits are checked on some paths and not others.

violates.other: ADR-0003:119-121 (the validator rejects '0'); CHANGELOG.md:4618-4620 (the Python mirror refuses what the server refuses); changeset.schema.json limits

root_causes.remedy: One validator per input kind at the shared write boundary (the server), the Python mirror generated from it, and a refusal with a validation code before the transaction starts.

root_causes.title: Resource bounds are not declared
root_causes.statement: Limits exist but are neither declared nor checked at the boundary: a combined key length for (s, p, o, graph), the subscript limit for a prefix, a ~35k-edge window cap under a migration, Python memory for an export claimed bounded, a Bolt session's IRIS connection, a latency budget.

violates.other: playbook §3.6 (capacity condition); SC budgets in specs 227 and 236

root_causes.remedy: Declare every bound (key lengths, prefix length, row caps, memory, connections, latency) in the contract, check it at the boundary with a named refusal, and test each at the limit.

root_causes.title: Parallel implementations of one operation diverge
root_causes.statement: One operation has several implementations (owner vs native PageRank, Arno vs fallback Leiden, the engine vs the sample API's Cypher entries, node vs edge/table vector search, the native gate vs the SQL path) with no differential test, and they answer differently.

violates.other: ALG-I1 (IVG answers the same without the library); ADR-0014:19; API-B5.8; spec 236 FR-014a

root_causes.remedy: One implementation per operation, or a differential test that runs every route on the same fixtures and compares answers.

root_causes.title: Progress is not designed for resumable or queued work
root_causes.statement: A bounded redaction re-scans from the first record on every call, and the embed queue serves PENDING entries in node-id order, so repeated work need not finish.

violates.other: LedgerRedact.cls:178-180 (running the same target again resumes it); progress premises PF-1..PF-4; HD-0604

root_causes.remedy: Persist the scan cursor with the marker so a resume continues, serve queues in arrival order, and add a progress test (a bounded run finishes in finitely many calls).

root_causes.title: Descriptions are written by hand and not checked against the code
root_causes.statement: Specs, ADRs, guides, docstrings and self-describing outputs (wire schema, SHOW CONSTRAINTS, STATUS_PARTS, TCK figures) are maintained by hand; they lag the code or state behaviour it does not have, and nothing fails when they drift.

violates.other: playbook §3.1 and §3.8 (every requirement carries evidence); docs/dev/TESTING_POLICY.md

root_causes.remedy: Generate or test every description: execute documentation examples (tests/docs), check spec and ADR status lines in CI, generate the wire schema, constraint lists and status parts from the code, and keep evidence claims tied to commits of this repository.

root_causes.title: Test, packaging and deploy tooling diverges from the product
root_causes.statement: The product's own fixtures, installers and entry points are not exercised as shipped: the test deploy compiles every class (unlike setup), two e2e fixtures read a meta key that does not exist, the bolt-on installer and the docker recipe do not do what the README says, declared console scripts cannot run.

violates.other: docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md:353 (Community is supported); deploy/README.md; pyproject.toml console scripts

root_causes.remedy: CI that installs from the built package, runs the deploy recipes and console scripts on Community, and fixtures that call the product's own setup and read its real keys.

root_causes.title: Stated refusals, options and protocol verbs are accepted and ignored
root_causes.statement: Interfaces accept inputs whose documented meaning they do not implement, instead of refusing them: a WHERE after RETURN, an unknown procedure, an untranslatable expression (NULL), a burst predicate, Leiden's max_levels/tol, suppress_reverse, a route timeout and cache flag, Bolt BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK and PULL {n}, transaction verbs on the embedded cursor, IVG_STRICT_NAMESPACE, --workers N, FHIR pagination, ACORN first, the metrics hook for every outcome, the MCP query text.

violates.other: playbook §5 lesson 'a refusal written in the spec is not a refusal'; CYP-X3.8, CYP-X10.2, CYP-X12.x; Bolt protocol (P-1612)

root_causes.remedy: Audit every documented refusal, parameter and protocol verb mechanically (a list generated from the docs and specs), implement it or refuse it with a named error, and test each.

root_causes.title: Stores have no enforced single write owner
root_causes.statement: Outside the ledger, stores owned by one module are written directly by others: ^KG("prop") has no owner and four writers, the Arno bridge moves the adjacency token, the vector module kills a sub-store of ^NKG, the Cypher DELETE and the SQL adapter delete vector, document and reification rows themselves, the FHIR build writes the label index and vector rows, a loader clears content tables by raw SQL. Each direct writer skips the owner's rules (routes, tokens, graph scope, strict mode).

violates.other: playbook §3.4 (each store has a single write owner); ADR-0011 (one adjacency writer); module Scope sections of the ontology

root_causes.remedy: Name one owner per store (as GraphStores.Inventory does for erasure) and route every other writer through the owner's method; a mechanical census (as the structural lane's st-check-own-census) that fails on a write to a store outside its owner.

root_causes.title: Bulk loads bypass the indexes and key checks every other path relies on
root_causes.statement: BulkLoader writes with INSERT %NOINDEX %NOCHECK by default: the rows it writes are in no index and pass no unique check until the indexes are rebuilt. Readers, the liveness check, erasure and the key invariants all read through those indexes, so duplicate keys are stored, a mode-off graph holds parallel rows, erasure leaves the loaded edge, and redaction completes while the tenant's loaded rows exist.

violates.other: schema.py:34-44, 396-419 (unique keys); GID-I4.10; spec 256 FR-005 (refuse while any row of the target is live); ADR-0004

root_causes.remedy: Make the bulk loader leave the indexes current before it returns (rebuild inside the load, or no %NOINDEX on key-carrying tables) and drop %NOCHECK for unique keys; until then refuse erasure and redaction while an index build is pending.

root_causes.title: Server answers are hand-encoded text decoded by patterns
root_causes.statement: Several ObjectScript methods answer Python with hand-built text (comma lists, partly escaped JSON, shape-sniffed maps), and the Python side repairs or decodes it by text patterns: a leading-dot patch rewrites ids, comma splitting breaks names, an unescaped control character breaks the JSON, a node named 'components' is read as a summary.

violates.other: TXT-B2.13 (each id and score in the answer is valid JSON); RFC 8259 escaping (CHANGELOG.md:463-467); the decoders' own docstrings

root_causes.remedy: One wire encoding for every server answer (%DynamicObject / JSON arrays built by the library, never by concatenation) decoded by json.loads only, with no text repair; a round-trip test with hostile names and ids.

excluded.title: In sync mode a failed build runs in the reader's own process
excluded.reason: not reproduced (b-09-f0904-sync-failed-build): a sync-mode failed build compiled in the reader's process, but the process still answered and prepared SQL on Community 2026.1; the harsher effect is a 2026.3 premise (P-0903); the compile-cost mechanism is source-confirmed (findings/audit/09.json)

excluded.title: The sample API lets two threads use its one IRIS connection at once
excluded.reason: not reproduced (c16-s3-graphql-sample-api): two threads and one query thread on the shared connection gave 0 wrong answers in 12 s on 2026.1 with driver 5.3.2; the missing lock is source-confirmed and the premise stays open (findings/audit/16.json)

excluded.title: The REST dispatcher may read only the first chunk of a large request body
excluded.reason: refuted on IRIS 2026.1 Community: its premise P-1607 (Read() with no length returns at most 32,000 characters) does not hold for the CSP request stream classes (c16-s5-fraud-sql-stream, c16-s8-followup; findings/audit/16.json); the end-to-end web check is blocked-access

excluded.title: Candidate: with the adjacency index declared, a failed rebuild could leave part of the adjacency missing
